doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

title: Writing on the road with a small battery keyboard
summary: He wrote in hotel rooms on a small keyboard that let him hear whole voicings.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So can I imagine you on the band bus with a score pad in front of you, could you write?

No I never really wrote on the bus while it was moving. I would do it in the hotel rooms. I’d do it when he had a break or a day off. I carried a little keyboard about this big, battery powered, that I had in my suitcase, which I still have. And I wrote with, up until about three or four years ago, until I finally broke down and learned some computer
programs. But that was my comfort — it sounded really bad but I knew if I could get a chord to sound really good on that thing, it would sound amazing with the band.

And the keys were small so I could fit the entire voicing within my two hands. I wouldn’t have a reach or hold the pedal down or anything, I could just do that and hear all the voices, which was really helpful for me.
I like that kind of story, that sort of low-tech, all you need is that little tool and it helps you to be creative.
